paper.title_en: Fluctuations and correlations of conserved charges in isobar collisions at <math altimg="si1.svg"><msqrt><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></msqrt></math> = 200 GeV with the STAR detector
paper.abstract_en: We report measurements of second-order cumulants and correlations of experimentally accessible baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness proxies in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions at <math altimg="si2.svg"><mrow><msqrt><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></msqrt><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow></math> GeV with the STAR experiment. The results exhibit similar centrality dependences in the two isobar systems within uncertainties. The baryon-strangeness correlation CBS is compared with lattice-QCD and UrQMD calculations. Motivated by recent lattice-QCD predictions for QCD matter in an external magnetic field, several ratios of conserved-charge correlations are studied as functions of centrality. In peripheral collisions, the measured ratios exhibit the same ordering as the lattice-QCD prediction. A qualitatively similar hierarchy is also found in UrQMD, although the model underpredicts the observed peripheral-to-central enhancement. These results motivate further quantitative studies of possible magnetic-field contributions and other sources of the observed centrality dependence.
